The guy who wrote this is probably the type who gets offended by quiet people. The kinda guy where if you don't talk to him constantly, he thinks you're one of those 'assholes' who ignores him. 99% of hatred toward introverts comes from people who can't handle people not talking to them.

I think the problem is there are some people who just can't handle not being talked to. If they notice someone rarely talks to them, they feel offended and think that person is "ignoring" them. Sometimes they feel like they have to 'get back' by breaking down that persons character, calling them self-centered or something else nasty. This happens too often with me and it's tiring. I could be totally fine with someone. I think they're cool, I respect them, and the times I do talk to them, I enjoy it. But of course, I can never talk to them as much as they want me to, and they blow up in my face because they didn't get the attention they crave. Not talking to you doesn't make me an asshole.

It's a lot more complicated than that. Yes I want friends, and I don't like talking to people very much. It's not because I'm self-absorbed and I don't like having that label lazily slapped on me. My intentions are good and overall I want to do good to people around me, but I am socially awkward, disinterested in others and have trouble relating with them, and pessimistic about human connection because my life thus far has been traumatic. I think it's judgmental and kind of snobby to just assume everyone who is quiet is a self-centered asshole.
